args.title: The int() helper uses Number.parseInt(raw, 10), which silently parses a
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

The int() helper uses Number.parseInt(raw, 10), which silently parses a value like "12h" or "1h" as 12 or 1 instead of rejecting it; it should validate that the entire string is a valid integer (e.g. using Number.isInteger(Number(raw)) or a regex match) and throw for any trailing non-numeric characters, so malformed TTL values like TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=12h fail fast at startup instead of being silently misread as minutes.

args.body:
label: bug
file: src/config.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.
src/config.ts's int(name, fallback) function does `Number.parseInt(raw, 10)` and only checks Number.isNaN(value); parseInt("12h", 10) returns 12 (not NaN), so TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=12h and RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=1h are read as 12 and 1 minutes respectively, matching the reported expiresInMinutes: 12 and the one-minute reset link expiry, with no startup error as the maintainer says there should be.

args.title: The readiness handler only maps checks.db === "down" to a non-200 respon
args.body:
File: src/api/health.ts

The readiness handler only maps checks.db === "down" to a non-200 response; a "degraded" overall status (e.g. queue backlog past QUEUE_DEGRADED_AT) still returns HTTP 200, so load-balancer probes that only look at the status code cannot distinguish degraded from healthy. Give "degraded" its own distinguishable HTTP status (or otherwise make the status code reflect the checks) so operators can configure the probe correctly.
